description: Trim orders (SPEC section 11.20), every one signed with SecretA of signatures.json for its app, generation 2, but where a case says otherwise. order: the file's order, Wappie's, issued at 2026-10-13T12:00:00Z: a deleted item purged, then a live one kept down to its floor; results' for_order cases are judged against it. orders: an order read as an app reads what the platform sends (members it does not know ignored, every member present, null only for floor), then Validate: order_id a UUIDv7; round 1 to 3; issued_at <= not_before < valid_until <= issued_at + 6 h; floor issued_at's UTC date less 90 days, or null, and then every keep step's keep_bytes 0; basis.measured_at under an hour before issued_at; 1 to 2000 steps, each item once, keep_bytes (0 to 2^53 - 1) exactly on keep; basis_purge naming exactly the purge steps' items; secret 1 or more; mac v1= and 64 lowercase hex. decisions: the order as the feed's document carries it (feed), what the app holds and sees, and its decision, in this order: check 1 on the feed's copy (contract.VerifyTrimOrder: the MAC under one of secrets, its app, workspace and generation the document's, and with floor null a plan source neither plan nor live_move), and when no secret it holds verifies that copy, check 4's GET first and check 1 on that answer's copy (no signed answer: wait); else refused invalid_order, recorded nowhere. An order whose order_id has a recorded result: resend, that result unchanged. Before valid_until (exclusive), wait while now is before not_before (inclusive) or generation_confirmed is false: no result, no record, no round. Then refused held (the allow shut, or a local brake holding the workspace at observe), refused expired (now at or after valid_until), check 4 (get: doc with get_doc, none, rate_limited, unavailable or not_found; no signed answer, rate_limited and unavailable wait; not_found, a document with no trim or another order_id, refused not_current; the same order_id: check 1 again on that copy, used from here), with a floor check 5 (basis, the report its basis names as the app kept it, null when it no longer does: usage_moved; else usage now within max(1 % of the GET's quota_bytes, 100 MB) of it, in total and for each step's item, a purge step whose item was purged already left out with its basis bytes; else usage_moved), check 6 (a step's item absent, or purged on a keep step: item_unknown; then per step: a purge step's item deleted with its basis_purge and a keep step's live run, else that step alone item_changed; a purge step whose item the app purged since: done with 0). steps: what a run does with each step. runs: an order the app took (order), and per step the events before it starts (before; none for the first) and between its batches (between): same (check 4's GET answered the same order_id), batch, report, purged_event and snapshot go on; none, rate_limited and unavailable wait, running nothing; expired, held, other, not_found, no_trim, feed_null and feed_other (the feed applied a document whose trim is null or another order) and interrupted stop the order with expired, held, not_current or interrupted; item: the step's item at its check 6 (as_ordered; changed: refused item_changed and the run goes on; purged_since: done with 0); bytes_after and at_floor (a keep step stopped at the floor above keep_bytes: partial). reported: the result the app reports, with usage_seq. results: a result decoded strictly, then Validate, and with for_order ValidateFor the file's order: outcome done (every step done), partial or refused; code one of not_current, expired, usage_moved, item_unknown, invalid_order, held on refused, null or one of held, expired, not_current, interrupted on partial, null on done; steps [] on refused, else each step once, outcome done, partial, refused (code item_changed) or not_run (only once the order stopped, and every step after it), bytes_after null on refused and not_run; usage_seq null exactly on refused; against the order: its order_id, its steps in its order, a purge step done at 0 bytes. answers: the platform's answer, read as an app reads what the platform sends, then Validate: accepted or duplicate with code null; rejected with invalid_request, not_found or conflict; order_id a UUID, or "" on a rejected invalid_request alone.
